mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, it signals a significant economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST declines > 10% YoY and UNRATE > 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing by more than 0.5% per month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals strengthening economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters.
